analysis.title: Hedge Funds Suffer DeepSeek-Sized Rout As Goldman Flags A $65 Billion CTA Trapdoor Under An S&P That "Barely Moved"
key_insights: The S&P fell less than 50bps on the week and sits 2.5% below its all-time high, but hedge fund portfolios took heavy losses beneath the index. On Thursday all three major hedge fund cohorts (Fundamental L/S, Systematic, Multi-Strats) lost more than 1% on the same day for the first time since COVID.

Goldman's Hedge Fund VIP long/short basket fell 4% on Thursday, a move only rivaled over the past decade by DeepSeek Monday and the COVID selloff. TMT-focused hedge funds are down 9.6% month-to-date and Asia Fundamental L/S is down 9.3%. TMT funds are still up 8% YTD and Systematic L/S is up 18.7%.

Coppersmith reads the move as an investor leverage unwind rather than an AI demand bubble bursting, with positioning moving much faster than fundamentals. Funds hedged their AI books without selling them, which helps explain why the pain has been persistent.

After Thursday's selling, hedge fund gross leverage was still 312% (96th percentile over five years). Fundamental net leverage fell to 47%, a one-year low, and the overall long/short ratio is in the 1st percentile on a five-year lookback.

Goldman's floor saw about $20bn of TMT selling over the past two weeks versus $23bn during July's AI unwind. SPX is down 2.4% this time versus 3.4% in July, so index damage is about 70% of July's while selling is about 87% of July's.
Goldman's AI Data Centers and US AI Inference baskets are down roughly 19% each over two weeks, worse than in July. The SOX is down 14% while the equal-weight S&P and US Defensives are up.

The episode overlay puts the market around day 10 of the unwind. In July the selling stopped around trading day 10 and stocks rallied. That is the bull case, with Coppersmith hoping for a better positioning equilibrium.

Goldman's CTA model has CTAs long $38.5bn of S&P futures (91st percentile), nearly 80% of aggregate net longs across the 21 markets tracked. The S&P is already below its short-term trend threshold, and the medium-term trigger is about 1.3% below Friday's close.

CTA flow asymmetry: in a flat tape CTAs sell about $11.6bn of S&P over the next week. Even a 2 standard deviation rally leaves them net sellers ($3.7bn). One month out, upside buying is $9bn against $65bn of downside supply, a ratio of more than 7 to 1.

Nasdaq CTA signals have deteriorated. CTAs are heavily short the Russell (2.5th percentile), and a 2SD rally over the next month would force $16.4bn of buying. Nomura's McElligott notes CTAs are positioned the opposite way in bonds, where a 2% rally would trigger roughly half a trillion dollars of systematic buying.

SPX vol is starting to react. Fixed-strike vol is catching a bid, downside skew and tails continue to outperform, and VIX positioning, particularly VIX vol, is becoming a bigger part of the conversation. Goldman's Vol Panic Index rose from 4.63 on Wednesday to 7.94 on Friday, reaching the 'panic' bogey for the first time since late July.

Within the Vol Panic Index, VIX vol is the most elevated component (8.94), followed by the 1m/3m ATM term structure (7.74). SPX skew eased from 8.88 to 7.62, and McElligott observed that puts were losing their bid. Every reading was below 3.5 a month ago.

Microsoft and Alphabet report Wednesday after the close, Amazon on Thursday, and the FOMC decision is also Wednesday. Coppersmith says the earnings matter more after Meta because of scrutiny of AI capex, funding needs and returns, and that the bar for reassurance has moved higher.

Meta's capex guide sent its CDS to a record. Goldman's trading floor lists three exits for the AI complex: cut capex, delay, or dilute. The AI financing story is moving from equities to credit, and hyperscaler funding commentary is expected to matter as much as cloud growth.
Options price slightly larger than average moves for the hyperscalers: MSFT 4.8% (vs 4.6% average realized), GOOGL 5.6% (5.2%), AMZN 7.5% (6.6%).

Goldman Korea strategists cut their 12-month KOSPI target from 12,000 to 9,000, still more than 60% upside from Friday's 5,550 close after a 40% correction. Coppersmith says at 4x forward earnings a lot of bad news on the memory cycle is priced in.

Brazil's runoff went to Lula (51.8% to 48.2% with 99.7% counted). Hyperliquid's Brazil ETF perpetual fell nearly 30%, and one local PM expects swap rates up 150-200bp and the real down about 10% on Monday.

Coppersmith leans toward a relief rally after two weeks of selling but holds the view loosely given elevated gross exposure, negative systematic flow asymmetry and geopolitical risks. His preferred expression is call spreads for defined downside. The author thinks a short-covering pop into Wednesday's earnings that gets sold is more likely than July's clean V.

tension_points.bull_case: Selling has been relentless for two weeks, nets are at a one-year low, and July's unwind ended around day 10 with a sharp rally. Goldman's Prime desk reads low nets as a buy-the-dip setup and Coppersmith sees room for a sharp reversal if earnings cooperate.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross leverage is still at the 96th percentile, CTAs have $65bn to sell below a trigger about 1.3% away, AI funding stress is spreading to credit, and Brazil is a fresh EM shock. The author expects a short-covering pop into earnings that gets sold.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The S&P breaking the medium-term CTA trigger about 1.3% below Friday's close, or hyperscaler earnings and funding commentary on Wednesday and Thursday failing to reassure.
